publication: Paul Fodor, Definite Logic Programs: Models, CSE 595 Semantic Web, Stony Brook University. Undated 19-slide author-hosted PDF, inspected 2026-10-23; slide numbers equal PDF pages.

reviews.checked_passages: Slides 3–10 and 12–19: definite clauses, Herbrand universe/base, model transfer, intersections, least-model ground consequences and immediate-consequence iteration. Slide 11 was inspected for its claimed boundary.
reviews.consumers: [First-order Horn rules](entries/first-order-horn-rules/entry.html), especially grounding, least models and the quantified-consequence counterexample.
reviews.outcome: FODOR-HORN-01 records the unrestricted consequence claim on slide 12. Adopt the transfer only for ground atoms, explicitly require a nonempty ground-term domain, and prove existence via intersections or the omega-stage construction. Finite termination requires a finite ground base; mathematical closure with functions need not terminate. The universal equality-free Herbrand theorem already supplies a broader sufficient class than definite clauses, despite slide 11 wording.
